comparator.name: Bachelor Taalwetenschap
comparator.sourceNotes: The current curriculum for students starting in 2026 defines a 180-EC bachelor comprising a 120-EC major and 60 EC of electives. The major contains two 30-EC first-year core profiles, one 30-EC specialisation, two compulsory methodology courses totalling 15 EC, a 7.5-EC capstone/preparatory course and a 7.5-EC BA thesis. The generic normalized target does not name a specialisation. Language and Cognition is selected because the programme overview defines Linguistics through how people speak and understand one another, how language works, language acquisition and processing in the brain; the selected package most broadly develops those defining questions without narrowing the route to Dutch-language society or computation. All eight first-year courses, both compulsory second-year methodology courses, the four-course Language and Cognition package, capstone, thesis and the complete 60-EC open elective space are represented. This route was fixed before UCR fit was assessed.
components: Capstone Course Linguistics: Research, Writing and Reflection
Genuine open space for a minor, a second specialisation or individual electives.

core: Linguistic structure, comparison and the scientific study of human language
Language acquisition, cognition, speech processing and human behaviour
Empirical, experimental, quantitative and digital methods for language research
Meaning, communication and language in social context
adjacent: Language, society, multilingualism, identity and mediated communication
Computational linguistics, formal language, artificial intelligence and language models
questions: How do people acquire, process and understand language?
How do language, identity and multilingual communities shape one another?
How can computation and AI model human language?

alternatives.label: Language, Cognition & Communication
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum is centred on cognition, psycholinguistics, development, meaning and communication, supported by empirical methods and humanities interpretation; the label names those actual curricular emphases.
alternatives.concept: The closest feasible UCR response to Linguistics: a language-and-cognition curriculum combining psycholinguistics, neuroscience, psychology, meaning, rhetoric, philosophy of mind, social context and empirical research.
progression: Foundational brain and behaviour, communication, data and social science precede perception, development, higher cognition, psycholinguistics and advanced research. Formal prerequisites and semester availability are satisfied.

alternatives.label: Language, Society, Media & Culture
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum concentrates on rhetoric, style, literature, media, sociology, history and cultural representation, so the label accurately describes a social and cultural communication route.
alternatives.concept: A distinct route generated by language-and-society evidence, studying meaning, rhetoric, multilingual social contexts, identity and cultural power through communication, literature, media, sociology and history.
progression: Introductory communication, literature, media, history and philosophy precede advanced textual meaning, persuasive communication, media, cultural research and interpretation. All assigned courses meet availability and prerequisite rules.
alternatives.distinctness: This route replaces most of the closest alternative’s neuroscience, psychology and cognitive-science sequence with a sustained curriculum in literature, media, history, sociology, rhetoric and cultural representation, changing well over 30 EC.

alternatives.label: Language, Computation & Artificial Intelligence
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum combines programming, language-relevant data science, machine learning, neural networks, logic, mathematics and AI with psycholinguistics and communication; the label reflects that actual mix.
alternatives.concept: A distinct computational-linguistics route combining programming, text and language data, machine learning, neural networks, logic, optimisation, mathematics and AI with psycholinguistics, cognition and meaning.
progression: Programming, data science and communication precede machine learning, AI, deep learning, optimisation, advanced cognition, psycholinguistics and statistical research. All formal prerequisites and semester offerings are satisfied.
alternatives.distinctness: This route replaces the society-and-media alternative’s literature, history, art and cultural-analysis sequence with programming, mathematics, machine learning, neural networks, optimisation and AI, while retaining psycholinguistics and meaning as the language-specific bridge.

routeSelection.basis: The generic target offers three specialisations. Language and Cognition best represents the programme’s broad defining questions about how people speak and understand one another, how language is acquired and how the brain processes language. It was selected independently of UCR fit; Taal en Samenleving and Language and Computation remain separately evidenced directions for UCR alternatives.

selection.assessment: The closest match owns the broad structural, cognitive, acquisition, meaning and communication evidence. Language, Society and Communication and Language, Computation and AI are included sequentially because each is an official, independently evidenced specialisation direction, can be implemented coherently at UCR and differs materially from the preceding alternative. All generator-eligible interests 16239–16258 are assigned either to the closest-match core or one of these two candidates. The three schedules contain exactly 24 courses/180 EC, satisfy prerequisite and semester availability constraints, include at least six level-300 courses and are pairwise distinct by substantially more than 30 EC.

notes.text: Utrecht Linguistics has a fixed 120-EC major with one 30-EC specialisation and 60 EC of genuine elective space. UCR uses a fully specified 24-course liberal-arts curriculum; the comparison preserves the comparator’s open elective space rather than inventing subjects for it.

UCR offers relevant psycholinguistics, communication, cognition, data and AI courses but no full sequence in phonetics, phonology, morphosyntax and formal linguistics, and no scheduled course is a BA thesis. These gaps remain explicit.
